reasoning: Recent Idaho polling and reporting indicate that the 2026 U.S. Senate race remains strongly Republican-leaning, but the margin has tightened from earlier 40+ point spreads to the mid‑single‑digits to mid‑20s depending on the pollster and field dates. A late July Change Research poll summarized by the New York Times shows Sen. Jim Risch leading independent Todd Achilles by roughly low‑20s margins (about R+22 to R+24), while a mid‑August Bullfinch Group/VoteHub poll has Risch ahead of Achilles by only 4 points (R+4), suggesting substantial volatility yet a persistent GOP edge in this ruby‑red state[1][8][11]. Structurally, Idaho’s statewide Cook Partisan Voting Index remains deeply Republican (about R+19), reinforcing that even with a competitive independent, the underlying environment strongly favors the GOP[5][9][13][15].

sources.name: The New York Times / Change Research
sources.details: The New York Times Senate polling page for Idaho reports Change Research polls conducted July 28-30 showing Sen. Jim Risch leading independent Todd Achilles by margins in the low 20s (around R+22 to R+24).

sources.name: PredictionHunt / Peak Insights
sources.details: PredictionHunt summarizes a June 2026 Peak Insights statewide poll with Risch at 55%, Democrat David Roth at 15%, and independent Todd Achilles at 7%, giving Risch a 40-point lead over the Democrat in a multi‑candidate field, indicating a noncompetitive baseline environment at that time.

sources.name: NBC News
sources.details: NBC News reports that Jim Risch won the May 19 Republican primary for U.S. Senate with about 67.3% of the vote, underscoring his strong standing within the GOP electorate ahead of the general election.

sources.name: Idaho Capital Sun
sources.details: Idaho Capital Sun reports that Democratic nominee David Roth ended his campaign for the U.S. Senate seat held by Risch on July 28, 2026, leaving independent Todd Achilles as the primary challenger.

sources.name: Roll Call
sources.details: Roll Call notes that Idaho Democrat David Roth dropped out of the Senate race, clearing a path for independent Todd Achilles to face Republican Sen. Jim Risch as the main challenger in the 2026 general election.

sources.name: Idaho Statesman
sources.details: The Idaho Statesman reports on David Roth’s exit and notes that most recent polls compiled by The New York Times still show Risch leading Achilles, though the size of the lead varies by poll.

sources.name: Politically.com / The Bullfinch Group / VoteHub
sources.details: Politically.com relays a Bullfinch Group / VoteHub Idaho poll with Jim Risch at 34%, Todd Achilles at 30%, and Matt Loesby at 4%, implying roughly an R+4 margin for Risch over Achilles in a three‑way general election field.
sources.date_range: August 2026 (exact dates not shown, poll released Aug. 16, 2026)

sources.name: Cook Political Report
sources.details: Cook Political Report’s Cook Partisan Voting Index map and related updates on X indicate that Idaho remains a strongly Republican state, with a statewide PVI of roughly R+19 for the current cycle, reflecting its long‑term GOP advantage.
